title: Catch the idea, then loop it
summary: In three short stops I show you how to catch an idea in one line, why a catch is not yet a brief, and why most ideas should stay in the inbox.

stops.title: Catch it in one line

beats.text: Once an AI does the typing, ideas arrive faster than you can build them. A thing that took a month takes an evening, so every annoyance becomes a project. Most of them vanish. You tell yourself you will remember, and then it is Thursday.

beats.quote: Keep the inbox ugly and the lines short.
beats.text: Keep the inbox somewhere you can reach from anywhere. A notes app on your phone, or a plain text file that syncs to it. Use whichever you will actually open, and keep it ugly and the lines short.

beats.quote: A catch that takes longer than ten seconds won't get done on the bus.
beats.text: The fix is one inbox you can reach from anywhere, and one line per idea. What it is, and the problem it solves if you know. Do not design it. A catch that takes longer than ten seconds will not get done on the bus.

runes.quote: A catch that takes longer than ten seconds won't get done on the bus.

stops.trial: For one day, write every idea down in one line, wherever you catch it, without judging any of them.
digest: Cheap building means more ideas than evenings, and most vanish.
Keep one inbox you can reach from anywhere, and write one line per idea.
Do not design it yet. A catch longer than ten seconds will not get done.

stops.title: A catch is not a brief

beats.quote: The line in your inbox is a catch, not a brief.
beats.text: Here is the mistake a cheap build tempts you into. The line in your inbox is a catch, not a brief. Paste it straight into an agent and you get something confident and a little beside the point. You get the teammate from the first note.

beats.quote: ask it to interview you, one question at a time
beats.text: So there is a step in between, and it is the one people skip. Pick one idea and turn it into the three-part brief. Ask your AI to interview you, one question at a time, until the brief is complete. Then you edit it, because that is where your judgment goes in.

beats.figure: From an idea to a built thing
beats.text: From there you know the path. Draw what needs drawing, write a plan with a done line per step, and build one step at a time. The inbox feeds the brief, the brief feeds the plan, and the plan feeds the loop.

runes.quote: The line in your inbox is a catch, not a brief.
ask it to interview you, one question at a time

stops.trial: Pick the idea that surprised you most and ask your AI to interview you into a three-part brief. Change one line and save it next to your plan.
digest: The line in your inbox is a catch, not a brief.
Pick one idea and ask your AI to interview you, one question at a time, until the brief is complete.
The inbox feeds the brief, the brief feeds the plan, and the plan feeds the loop.

stops.title: Most ideas stay in the inbox

beats.quote: most of your ideas should never get built
beats.text: An inbox that only grows is a guilt pile, so here is the hard part. Most of your ideas should never get built. Look at the list a week later and a lot of them already look smaller. That is the inbox working. Let them die cheaply.

beats.quote: one active project at a time
beats.text: One rule worth trying: one active project at a time, with one next step you could start in ten minutes. Everything else waits. When you are tempted by a second thing, add a line instead.

beats.quote: a beautiful inbox and nothing shipped
beats.text: And where I might be wrong. A tidy capture habit can turn into procrastination, a beautiful inbox and nothing shipped. And some ideas are better chased the minute they show up. Find the number of projects that does not leave you feeling behind.

runes.quote: most of your ideas should never get built
one active project at a time

stops.trial: Keep the inbox going for a week, then delete the ideas that already look smaller, and tell me which one you were glad to delete.
digest: An inbox that only grows is a guilt pile.
Most of your ideas should never get built, so let them die cheaply.
Try one active project at a time. When you are tempted by a second, add a line instead.
